2026-10-29. ACCEPTED at 0<eta<=1 and the explicitly memoryless full-channel scope. Current author files are frozen and bound in the receipt. The separately accepted flagged-continuity addendum gives the sharper normalization statement.

## Argument checked independently
1. On the shared finite support, rho_b^{-1/2}rho_a rho_b^{-1/2} has strictly positive finite minimum/maximum eigenvalues. Tensoring a fixed payload/reference state and applying the same CP successful processor preserves both order inequalities. Positive operators bounded above and below by positive multiples have equal kernels. Distinct unitary CHANNEL Choi rays therefore cannot both be produced with nonzero heralded weight. Global-phase differences are not distinct channels. Pure nonorthogonal program states have different supports and are not ruled out.

2. Write N_a=l N_b+D with D CP. Expand the fixed adaptive N-slot successful comb multilinearly; the all-N_b term is l^N E_b and every other term is CP. The upper inequality follows analogously from u N_b-N_a CP. Remainder maps need not be trace nonincreasing; their positivity under the finite network suffices. Coherent protected memory, payload already present, measurements and feed-forward do not invalidate this. The circuit must be the SAME known circuit for both hypotheses.

3. For unbounded but almost-sure finite stopping, group all successful outcomes by stopping depth N. Each depth aggregate is a CP finite-slot map; continuous measurement outcomes can be integrated inside that aggregate, so only the depth decomposition need be countable. A positive countable sum supported on one ray forces every summand onto that ray. Positive total success has at least one nonzero finite-depth summand. Its comparable counterpart at the other source cannot fit a distinct exact ray. No uniform positive lower comparison constant across all N is claimed or needed. Finite-dimensional memory at each finite depth suffices; genuinely infinite-depth output lies outside this argument.

## Load-bearing proof
Use unnormalized Choi convention J(D)=I/d_out and Tr J(N)=d_in. Positivity implies J(N)<=d_in I=(d_in d_out)J(D). For every finite N-slot acquisition network, inserting CP-order comparisons one slot at a time yields domination of every measurable classical output event by (d_in d_out)^N times its probability under replacement source D. Postselection, coherent intermediate workspace, continuous outcomes and adaptive choices are positive supermap operations and preserve this inequality. Initial trusted resources must not contain an extra unknown-source-dependent state or perfectly informative classical prior.

Include the stopping depth in the classical record. Let mu_theta,N be its subprobability measure. For each record r, the declared successful execution map has a measurable positive Choi matrix J_r, determined by the record and the fixed processor, not secretly by theta. Any additional known execution randomness can either be integrated into this CP map or included in the record. Trace-nonincreasing execution gives a bounded finite-dimensional Choi field. Nontermination of execution simply contributes no successful output.

If the aggregate successful Choi equals p_theta P_theta for a unitary ray P_theta and p_theta>0, then Tr[(I-P_theta) integral J_r dmu_theta]=0. The integrand is nonnegative, so it vanishes almost everywhere. Positivity then forces J_r to have support in the unitary ray, including elimination of its off-diagonal blocks. A positive aggregate trace means the set of records with nonzero J_r on this ray has positive mu_theta measure. A positive total over countably many finite stopping depths has some positive finite-depth contribution. Domination gives positive mu_D,N measure for that same fiber.
